name: Try Every Start
summary: From each start index, extend a run to the right as long as the characters stay unique; track the longest run seen.
visualizationIntent: init: show s and a longest-so-far of 0. loop: the i cursor fixes a start; the j cursor extends the run while characters are unique. check: when j hits a character already in the run, stop and compare this run's length to the best; the best run stays highlighted green. return: the longest run length.

lineExplanations.4: The longest unique run found so far.
lineExplanations.5: Where that best run starts (for highlighting).
lineExplanations.6: Start index of the current run.
lineExplanations.8: The set of characters currently in the run (as a string).
lineExplanations.9: The length of the current run.
lineExplanations.10: The run's right edge begins at the start.
lineExplanations.11: Extend the run to the right while possible.
lineExplanations.13: Check whether that character is already in the run.
lineExplanations.14: If it repeats, the run must stop here.
lineExplanations.16: Otherwise add the new unique character to the run.
lineExplanations.19: If this run beats the best, record it.
lineExplanations.21: Remember where the best run starts.
lineExplanations.22: Move to the next start index.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def lengthOfLongestSubstring(self, s): receives the string s.
syntaxExplanations.3: n = len(s) stores the string length.
syntaxExplanations.4: best = 0 starts the longest run at zero.
syntaxExplanations.5: best_start = 0 records where the best run begins.
syntaxExplanations.6: i = 0 sets the first start index.
syntaxExplanations.7: while i < n: tries every start.
syntaxExplanations.8: seen = "" holds the characters currently in the run.
syntaxExplanations.9: length = 0 counts the current run length.
syntaxExplanations.10: j = i places the run's right edge at the start.
syntaxExplanations.11: while j < n: extends the run rightward.
syntaxExplanations.12: ch = s[j] reads the next character.
syntaxExplanations.13: is_dup = ch in seen is True when the character already appears in the run.
syntaxExplanations.14: if is_dup: is true when the character repeats.
syntaxExplanations.15: break stops the run at the first repeat.
syntaxExplanations.16: seen = seen + ch adds the unique character to the run.
syntaxExplanations.18: j = j + 1 advances the right edge.
syntaxExplanations.19: if length > best: is true when this run is the longest so far.
syntaxExplanations.20: best = length records the new best length.
syntaxExplanations.21: best_start = i records where the best run starts.
syntaxExplanations.22: i = i + 1 moves to the next start.
syntaxExplanations.23: return best hands back the longest run length.
